metadata.title: The Three-Dimensional Counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture: Exact Validation, a Proved Seed-Family Constructor, the Discriminant Wall of Non-Properness, and Planar Equivariant Rigidity
metadata.description:
On 2026-07-20, Levent Alpöge announced (crediting the language model Claude Fable 5) a polynomial map F from C^3 to C^3 with constant Jacobian determinant -2 and a repeated value, refuting the Jacobian conjecture for every N ≥ 3. In exact arithmetic, the fiber over the announced target consists of exactly the three announced points. The map is a weighted skew product over the invariants v = xy, t = x^2 z; its Keller property is a two-variable identity and its fibers are governed by a cubic.

We prove a constructor: every admissible seed polynomial p, scale k and section q gives a Keller map of determinant -k p(1)^2 and generic fiber degree deg p + 1, with rational collisions in fiber degrees 3 to 6. The degree law (5d - 3, 5d - 4, 4) is machine-verified on four seeds; its extension to every seed and the minimality of the announced map within the family are conjectural. The asymptotic variety of F is the discriminant surface 27A^2C^2 - 18ABC + 16A + B^3C - B^2 = 0 and the plane C = 0 is not asymptotic; the image of F is the complement of an explicit curve, and over the reals the surface separates three real preimages from one.

In dimension two, equivariant Keller maps are linear for opposite-sign weights and affine, (f0 x, g0 y + c) or its swap, for one zero weight, so a planar counterexample must be non-equivariant; this agrees with Shaska's independent classification. Computations are exact; each result is marked machine-verified, derived or conjectural.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/algebraic-geometry/jacobian-conjecture).
metadata.version_notes: Full revision. Adds a related-work section, a methods section with four algorithms (exact validation, constructor with collision engineering, real census, equivariant enumeration), tables of the instances, the collisions, the census and the weight-system survey generated from the stored outputs, figures of the degree law, the fiber polynomial, the discriminant wall and the enumeration window, and a validation section per result. Proves the constructor theorem and the skew-product lemma. States the degree law as verified on four seeds and its extension and the minimality of the announced map as a conjecture. Gives the fibers over the plane C = 0; corrects the asymptotic variety to the discriminant surface alone and describes the image of the map as the complement of an explicit curve. Gives a complete proof of the planar equivariant classification, including the swapped affine form for one zero weight. Updates the discussion with the Mathieu range N ≥ 15, the Poisson conjecture for indices n ≥ 2 and the smallest known witness dimensions.
